analysis: Both changed files are documentation only (docs/architecture/hardware-support.md and docs/architecture/inference.md, the latter a metadata unit plus one patch). No source code, keys, attestation or authorization logic changed, so no control was weakened. The inference.md patch (hunk @@ -68,6 +68,221) adds a GLM5Next implementation-boundary section. It describes provider-side behavior: exact catalog gating (glm-5.3-flash), M5 Max/Ultra with 256 GiB, an identity chain (catalog pin, revision receipt, per-file manifest hash), a template allowlist (GLM5NextLocalQualification.requireShippedTemplate), an exclusion of media requests from prefix lookup and capture (CBv2Request.permitsHybridCheckpoint), and retained-fault quarantine on unproven retirement. The patch says the GLM execution policy is part of the encrypted checkpoint storage identity, which is consistent with the T-041 cache binding and does not alter it. The documentation also states that a local qualification selection cannot change coordinator advertisement. It is documentation, not an enforced control, and the review did not verify the claimed code behavior. hardware-support.md is a head-text view with no diff supplied, so the changes within it are not identifiable. Its content (memory cap arithmetic, process-ledger ownership, calibration and the cross-repo agreement note) makes no new trust claims and keeps backend links pinned to an immutable commit. Possible follow-up for the next pass: T-041 and TB-007 may merit a mention that GLM media requests skip prefix-cache reuse, and that a GLM execution policy keys the SSD cache storage identity. Those are optional documentation updates, not regressions. No cross-file security interaction was found.
